name: Day3: newsletters billed by list size

product.name: Day3
product.summary: Day3 is an email platform that only does the email part of a newsletter: their own domain, a signup form, the newsletter itself and good inbox placement. It bills by emails sent, never by list size.
product.offer: Unlimited subscribers on every plan, priced by the emails sent each month. The sender does the move for them by hand, at no cost: their export or a one click import from beehiiv, Kit, Mailchimp or MailerLite comes over with unsubscribes kept unsubscribed, the sending domain is set up and the template rebuilt.
product.audience: Independent newsletters that mostly just send email and sell their own sponsors: local news digests, niche and hobby newsletters, small businesses and creators with a list.
product.prices:
Billed by emails sent a month, with unlimited subscribers on every plan. Each plan covers up to its number of emails:
up to 1,000 emails a month: $1; up to 5,000: $3; up to 10,000: $5; up to 25,000: $8; up to 50,000: $14; up to 100,000: $25; up to 250,000: $60; up to 500,000: $115; up to 1,000,000: $220.
Emails a month are the list size times the issues a month: weekly is about 4.3 issues, twice a month 2, daily about 30. Pick the smallest plan whose number is at or above the total, never one below it: 10,000 readers weekly is about 43,000 emails, the $14 plan; 10,000 readers daily is about 300,000 emails, above 250,000, so the $115 plan.
The move to Day3 costs nothing.
product.pitch: beehiiv raised its prices in October 2026. Existing paid accounts pay the new price from their first renewal after 1 November 2026, often 30 to 50% more, with the biggest jumps between 10,000 and 50,000 subscribers. Kit, Mailchimp and MailerLite charge by list size, so the bill grows with the list even when the sending does not. Name their platform only when the signal names it, and never guess their list size: use a number they publish, or frame the price as an example. Day3 fits a newsletter that only needs to send. It has no ad network, referral program, paid subscriptions or web archive, so never claim it replaces those. The sender is Morten, who builds Day3: write as him, in the first person (I build Day3, I move the list), never about Morten in the third person.

steps.brief: A short personal note to the person who runs this newsletter, greeted by first name. Open on one recent thing they wrote or did (an issue, a story, a piece of news, a milestone) and react to it the way a reader would, in a sentence or two: congratulations, thanks, or what stayed with you. Never sum up what an issue covers. Then the reason to write in one sentence, from the signal: for beehiiv, the renewal price rise after 1 November; for Kit, Mailchimp or MailerLite, that they pay by list size. Then Day3 in one sentence with one example price for a list like theirs, framed as an example unless they publish their numbers. Close with one plain yes or no question about that price, on its own line, such as whether a price like that would be of any use to them. No questions about their list, their send day or their plans. 45 to 90 words. Vary the shape: not every email opens the same way or has the same paragraphs.

A short second note in the same thread, by first name, from one new angle: the move is done for them at no cost (their export or a one click import, unsubscribes kept, their domain set up, their template rebuilt), or what Day3 does not do (ad network, referrals, paid subscriptions) so they can judge the fit. One plain yes or no question about the offer, or none. 25 to 50 words.
